predecessors.name: Belgian Congo
predecessors.text: the Congo: 'The Belgian Congo achieved independence on 30 June 1960 under the name Republic of the Congo.'

ledger.x: 1960: the Congo becomes independent from Belgium.
1960: Antoine Gizenga's Free Republic of the Congo takes Orientale.
24 December 1960: 'Stanleyville troops occupied Bukavu and arrested the local army commander.'
January 1961: 'Gizenga's authority was also established over the Sankuru District of Kasai Province.'
By 10 January 1961 'control had been consolidated in Goma and the northern Kivu region.'
October 1961: 'Pro-Gizenga administrators were installed in the Maniema and Sankuru districts.'
1962: the central army enters Bakwanga and South Kasai's secession ends.
1964: the Simba rebellion takes the east and north.
ledger.cp: People's Republic of the Congo (Simba rebels)
People's Republic of the Congo (Simba rebels)

ledger.x: 1971: Mobutu renames the country the Republic of Zaire.
1996: the First Congo War begins in the east.
ledger.cp: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL)

ledger.x: 1997: the AFDL takes the whole country.
ledger.cp: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL)

ledger.x: 1997: Zaire is renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo under Laurent-Désiré Kabila.
1998: the Second Congo War divides the country.
ledger.cp: RCD and MLC rebels with Rwanda and Uganda

ledger.x: 2003: a unified transitional government ends the war.
ledger.cp: RCD and MLC rebels with Rwanda and Uganda

wars.name: Congo Crisis
wars.outcome: Infobox: 'The Congo established as an independent unitary state under the authoritarian presidency of Mobutu Sese Seko.'

wars.name: Simba rebellion
wars.outcome: The army and mercenaries retook Stanleyville soon after Operation Dragon Rouge of 24 November 1964, 'putting an end to the Simba rebellion'.

wars.name: First Congo War
wars.outcome: 'Mobutu fled Kinshasa on May 16'; Laurent-Désiré Kabila proclaimed himself president on 17 May 1997 and Zaire was renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

wars.name: Second Congo War
wars.outcome: Infobox 'Military stalemate'; Lusaka Ceasefire signed July 1999, Pretoria Accord 30 July 2002, Luanda Agreement 6 September 2002, Transitional Government 18 July 2003 with Joseph Kabila as president.

certainty.note: The international frontier is the colonial line inherited from the Belgian Congo (no border page was opened, so this rests on the dossier belgian-congo and the absence of any dispute on the DRC page).
